A Rally Without an Audience

Bitcoin advanced quietly on Tuesday, closing near $76,300 after touching an intraday high of $76,927. Volume came in below the seven-day average, indicating that few market participants followed the move.

The momentum came from traditional markets: the Nasdaq rose 2.63% and the S&P 500 gained 1.39%, lifting risk assets. The dollar remains weak, with the DXY holding steady around 98 — a level that has historically favored Bitcoin. US-Iran tensions remain on the radar, with JD Vance canceling his trip to Pakistan amid escalating diplomatic tensions, limiting risk appetite in crypto.

The bullish scenario we mapped out yesterday partially materialized: support in the $73,000 range held firm and Bitcoin reached $76,927, less than $100 away from the $77,000 target we had projected. In the bigger picture, price remains 13% below the 50-week EMA, confirming that the recovery is unfolding within a bearish market structure.
The $78,000 Gate

The trigger for continued upside is a breakout above the $78,000 resistance — a level that rejected price last Friday when Bitcoin hit $78,322 and reversed. A daily close above that level with above-average volume would open the path to $80,000.

If Bitcoin clears $80,000, the next target would be in the $82,500 range, where the 100-week EMA sits. Reclaiming that moving average would shift the market classification from confirmed bearish to caution zone — an important step in the structural recovery.

The catalysts that could unlock this scenario include a de-escalation of US-Iran tensions, continued institutional flows like those from Strategy, and futures positioning: with most traders positioned short (long/short ratio at 0.86), any upside breakout could trigger a liquidation cascade that accelerates the move.
The $73,000 Risk

Support at $73,800 has been tested five times in recent weeks and held every time. Each test, however, weakens the level. A daily close below that mark would send Bitcoin toward the $70,500 area, a support zone tested in early April.
If $70,500 fails to hold, the next target would be around $68,400, where the 200-week EMA sits — the last long-term support before the cycle floor.

Risks that could trigger this scenario: military escalation between the US and Iran in the Strait of Hormuz, a reversal of Bitcoin ETF flows, or higher-than-expected US employment and inflation data. In the crypto ecosystem, the transfer of 1.32 million Solana to exchanges signals potential selling, and the $292 million attack on KelpDAO adds caution to the DeFi segment.
Weekly Radar

The levels to watch are clear: resistance at $78,000 on the upside and support at $73,800 on the downside. Bitcoin is compressed between these two levels, and a breakout in either direction should define the path for the coming days. The daily RSI sits at 68, approaching the zone that signals price stretched in the short term.

On the calendar, the next FOMC meeting is on May 7. Until then, the US-Iran geopolitical factor will be the main external catalyst. For the long-term investor, price remains 11.5% above the 200-week EMA, the last structural support of the cycle.
